target.title: fix(ui): keep Worktree mutation errors visible
target.body:
Closes #106158

## What Problem This Solves

Worktree create, restore, delete, force-delete, and garbage-collection failures vanished from the Control UI before users could read them. Each mutation stored its error and then immediately ran `worktrees.list`; that refresh cleared the shared error state before rendering.

## Why This Change Was Made

Post-mutation reconciliation now preserves the mutation error while a successful list refresh updates the rows. A list refresh failure still replaces the earlier mutation error because the page can no longer claim its displayed state is current. Ordinary page loads and connection-driven refreshes keep their existing clear-at-start behavior.

This keeps the contract at the Worktrees page owner boundary and applies uniformly to every mutation finalizer rather than special-casing restore.

## User Impact

When a Worktree operation fails, the actionable Gateway error remains visible after the automatic row refresh. The user can retry from the up-to-date table. If reconciliation itself fails, the page shows that newer list error instead.

## Evidence

- Real authenticated Gateway + Playwright reproduction on current `main`: created and deleted a disposable Worktree, made its source repository unavailable, clicked Restore, observed the Gateway rejection and successful follow-up `worktrees.list`, then confirmed `.callout.danger` count remained zero. Restored the source and fully removed the disposable Gateway registry/snapshot state afterward.
- Blacksmith Testbox run `29235773032`: path-scoped changed checks passed.
- `ui/src/pages/worktrees/worktrees-page.test.ts`: 12/12 passed, including preserved mutation error and refresh-error replacement.
- `ui/src/e2e/worktrees.e2e.test.ts`: Chromium 1/1 passed through the rendered Settings > Worktrees Restore flow.
- Fresh autoreview: no actionable findings; confidence 0.94.
- `git diff --check`: clean.

No config, protocol, dependency, or migration change.
